summary: Built shopcli, a stdlib-only Python 3 package whose Shop().run(script) executes a flat inventory command language (item.add/remove/list, price.set/get, report.stock/margin, repeat N: prefixes) and answers with one reply shape {ok, results, warnings, error}. Every failure — parser, binder, kernel or host exception — becomes one Refusal record (code from a closed list, message, operation path ending in ✗, the agent's line, valid alternatives, concept hint, fix written in the agent's own line structure, host_name only for E_HOST), produced by an ordered suggester (namespace fact, mined redirect table, budgeted near spelling) plus a fix renderer that rewrites only the failing span. Warnings are raised at the agent's line, folded per line with a count, and results/warnings produced before a failure are still delivered.

pattern_mapping.Refusal: shopcli/refusal.py: frozen Refusal(code, message, path, where, valid, hint, fix, host_name) with to_dict(); its __post_init__ enforces the closed code, a path ending in ✗, and host_name only for E_HOST
pattern_mapping.Code list: shopcli/codes.py: CODES (9 codes), CODES_DOC documenting each once, WARNING_CODES ('RANGE'), check_code(); proven live by shopcli/docs.py examples run in tests/test_codes.py
pattern_mapping.Fix renderer: shopcli/fix.py: replace_command() and rename_key() slice the raw line at parser-recorded offsets so only the failing token changes; changed_span() exposes the minimal diff for tests; no fix is produced when a value would have to be invented
pattern_mapping.Suggester: shopcli/suggest.py: suggest_command() (namespace fact → redirect table → budgeted near spelling) and suggest_option(); the chapter's cross-kind step is deliberately skipped for a flat command language; distances/budget in shopcli/errors.py
pattern_mapping.Redirect table: shopcli/registry.py: Registry.redirects (rm, delete, ls, inventory) held on the registry instance and checked against the commands at load by Registry.validate()
pattern_mapping.Translator: shopcli/engine.py: Shop._translate() turns any non-Failure Python exception into E_HOST keeping type(exc).__name__ in host_name and adding the concept hint from Registry.host_hints (ZeroDivisionError in report.margin)
pattern_mapping.Site tracker: shopcli/parse.py: the parser's line number is the site — ParsedLine.where gives {line, source} and repeat prefixes are kept as path labels; no stack walking (note 6)
pattern_mapping.Warning folder: shopcli/warnings.py: WarningFolder folds identical warnings by (code, line, message) into one record with count; engine emits usual-range RANGE warnings per run so repeat N folds to count N
pattern_mapping.Binder/evaluator (Collaborations 1): shopcli/engine.py: Shop._resolve/_bind/_coerce build refusals with code, message, path and line, then run the handlers; _refuse() is the single place a Refusal is built

notes_applied: Note 1 (mine redirects, decide what a redirect does): the four names in TASK.md are refused with a concept hint and a literal fix rather than aliased, so the agent learns the real name in one round trip and no value has to be invented.

Note 2 (one fixed suggestion order, budget on the differing segment): namespace fact (E_NAMESPACE) → redirect table → near spelling with max(1, min(3, len/3)) applied to the verb or key only, so item.drop and item.add do not look close; the fourth cross-kind step is skipped for a flat command language.

Note 3 (fixes are code, only the failing part changes): fixes are produced by slicing the raw line at command/key offsets, so repeat N: prefixes, argument order and spacing survive; tests assert the changed span lies inside the failing token and the prefix is never dropped.

Note 4 (one shape and one closed code list for every layer): parser, binder, kernels and host all raise the same Failure type and pass through Shop._refuse; Refusal rejects unknown codes and a host_name on any code but E_HOST.
Note 5 (the path is part of the message): path is [repeat labels…, command, ✗ failing-part] so the agent sees which operation and which step of a chain failed.
Note 6 (the line is in the agent's program): where = {line, source} taken from the script line itself, including the repeat prefix, never an engine location.

Note 7 (warn at the line, fold repeats): RANGE warnings record the line and are folded by (code, line, message) with a count; qty outside 0–1000 warns but runs, and over-removal warns stating exactly what was done.

Note 8 (deliver what was produced before the failure): results and warnings are appended as they happen and the reply still carries them when an error stops the script, including partial runs of a repeat.

Note 9 (one redirect table per registry, checked at load): redirects, commands and host hints are instance state validated by Registry.validate(); tests show two registries do not share a table and a broken redirect fails at load.

Note 10 (never invent a value): wrong type, out-of-range and missing-option failures carry a hint with non-binding placeholders (<whole number>) and no fix; unknown names that are too far get valid alternatives and no fix.

Note 11 (test codes and fixes): shopcli/docs.py holds a runnable example per code and per fix; tests assert each code is raised by exactly its example, each redirect and templated fix binds in the same setup, and each fix differs from the agent's line only in the failing part.

Deviations recorded in the diary: distance is optimal-string-alignment Damerau–Levenshtein so one transposition counts as one edit (plain Levenshtein would refuse qyt → qty), and TASK.md's open behaviours were fixed as price.set on an unknown item → E_NOT_FOUND and over-removal → clamp to 0 with a RANGE warning.
tests: 108 tests across 11 modules under tests/ (codes, parse, commands, refusals, fixes, warnings, registry, host, repair loop, docs/doctest, invariants); last run: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → Ran 108 tests in 0.218s, OK. Two intermediate runs failed first (96 tests, 6 failures, all wrong test expectations about redirect arguments and minimal diff spans) and were fixed before finishing.
chapter_feedback: Helped most: the Structure table and the sketch, which mapped almost one-to-one onto modules and functions; the ordered suggester (note 2) was the single most useful rule, and skipping the cross-kind step for a flat language was stated explicitly enough to act on.
Helped: note 3's warning that four of five builds dropped a repeat prefix — it made me store raw offsets in the parser, which is why every fix in this build keeps its prefix and spacing.
Helped: note 10 (never invent a value) gave a clear rule for E_ARG_TYPE/E_ARG_RANGE/E_ARG_MISSING, including the idea of placeholders that cannot bind.

Misled slightly: the edit budget max(1, min(3, len/3)) with plain Levenshtein cannot suggest the most common typo (a transposition, qyt → qty), so the chapter's own example-adjacent intent needed a different distance metric; the chapter says only 'edit distance', so I chose Damerau–Levenshtein and documented the deviation.

Left to guess: the status of names agents typed — note 1 allows refusing with a fix, running as an alias, or running with a warning, and TASK.md only says 'treat them as known near-misses'; I refused, but a grader expecting alias-runs-with-warning would see different replies.

Left to guess: what to do when several arguments are wrong at once; the chapter's 'precision against noise' implies one failing part per refusal, which is what I did, but agents pay an extra round trip per bad key.

Left to guess: whether the fourth suggester step is ever safe in a language where two commands share an option name (e.g. name= on every command) — the chapter says skip it in a flat language, but 'flat' is not defined.

Minor friction: the chapter's 'valid: a handful, nearest first, only when nothing answers' is ambiguous about which names count as nearest for dotted commands; I rank on the verb first, then the namespace.
